translations.text: We read that when Saint Boniface was pope in Rome, he asked the emperor Phocas [?] to give him a house in Rome which people formerly called the Pantheon,
because all the idols used to be worshipped in it. When he had given it to him, he consecrated it to the honour of our Lord and of our Lady Saint Mary
and of all Christ's martyrs, so that just as the multitude of devils had formerly been worshipped in it, the memory of all God's saints would now be celebrated in it.
He then commanded that all the people should come to church on the day when the Kalends of November begins. And when the holy service had all been completed there,
each person returned home glad and happy. And from this arose the custom that today, throughout the whole world, people celebrate the memory of all God's saints,
so that whatever we have neglected in the whole year, we may make it all good today, and that we may come to eternal life through the intercession of the saints, with the help of our Lord.
